rejected.title: Aesthetic qualities
card: Aesthetic qualities are the features that make a text striking or beautiful to read or hear. They appeal to the senses and feelings, not only to the facts.
Rhythm
the pattern of beats and pauses in the words. Short, sharp lines can feel tense. Long, flowing lines can feel calm.
Imagery
language that helps a reader see, hear, touch, smell or taste something. In "the cold, grey sea hissed on the shingle", the sights and sounds make the scene feel real.
Shape
how a text is laid out, such as the length of its lines, its stanzas or its use of white space. A poem with one very short line can make that line stand out.
rejected.remember: Aesthetic qualities, such as rhythm, imagery and shape, make a text striking and add to its meaning.

a.q: Which of these best describes what aesthetic qualities do in a text?
opts: They make the text striking and add to its meaning
They give the reader facts that can be checked
They show which characters are on the writer's side
They list the events of the plot in order
a.why: Aesthetic qualities such as rhythm, imagery and shape make a text striking to read, and they shape the meaning a reader takes from it. Giving facts is not their purpose, because they work on the senses and feelings.
a.clue: Think about how a text feels as well as what it says.

b.q: Jai writes a poem about a storm. The first lines are long and slow. Then one line of two words stands alone on the page: "It broke." Which aesthetic quality does the lone short line mainly use?
opts: Shape, as the short line stands out on the page
Imagery, as it helps the reader smell the storm
Rhythm, as it makes every line flow smoothly
Rhythm, as it makes all the lines the same length
b.why: The line is set apart by its length and its place on the page, so its shape makes it stand out. Rhythm is also touched, but the short line breaks the flow rather than making it smooth, and the lines are not the same length. The line has no sense detail, so it is not imagery.
b.clue: Look at how the line sits on the page compared with the others.

version.title: Aesthetic qualities
card: Aesthetic qualities are the features that make a text striking or beautiful to read, such as its rhythm, imagery and shape. They also add to what the text means.
Rhythm
the pattern of beats and pauses in the words. Short, quick beats can feel urgent, and long lines can feel calm, so the sound can match the action.
Imagery
words that appeal to the senses. "Frost crunched under our boots" lets a reader hear and feel the cold, so the scene feels real.
Shape
how a text looks on the page, such as line length, gaps and stanzas. A poem about rain might fall down the page one word per line, so the layout acts out the idea.
version.remember: Ask how a text sounds, feels and looks, then how that adds to its meaning.

a.q: A poem about a lift going down sets one word on each line, so the words drop down the page. Which aesthetic quality is the poet using?
opts: Shape, through how the words sit on the page
Imagery, through words that appeal to the senses
Rhythm, through a steady pattern of beats
Rhyme, through words with the same end sound
a.why: The words are arranged so the layout itself moves downward, which is shape. Imagery comes from sense detail in the words, not from where they sit on the page.
a.clue: Think about how the poem looks, not how it sounds.

b.q: In Leo's poem about a storm, the lines rush along in short, quick beats. Once the storm passes, the poem slows into long lines. How does this rhythm add to the meaning?
opts: The pace of the lines mirrors the storm, then the calm
The long lines let the reader see the storm's colours
The quick beats make the storm seem calm and gentle
The change in pace shows the poet lost track of rhythm
b.why: The quick beats feel urgent like the storm, and the long lines slow down as it ends, so the sound acts out what happens. Seeing colours would be imagery, which comes from sense detail, not from the pace of the lines.
b.clue: How does the speed of the lines compare with the weather?

a.best: Shape, through how the words sit on the page

b.best: The pace of the lines mirrors the storm, then the calm
